newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines confirms 6-7 pct inflation goal for 97.
newsitem.headline: Philippines confirms 6-7 pct inflation goal for 97.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday the 1997 inflation target of six to seven percent had been confirmed in the regular review of a visiting six-man team of the International Monetary Fund.
With seven percent inflation targetted for the year end, the Central Bank will ensure that the declining trend is maintained by keeping a 5.0 to 6.0 percent inflation target next year, he said.
The Central Bank had kept monetary aggregates below the ceilings under the IMF-supported monetary programme in 1996, he said.

"In December 1996, the Philippine Central Bank's main operating targets of base money and reserve money were more than 20 billion pesos below the programme ceilings with the IMF," Singson said in a statement.
On the external front, the country's gross international reserves, which stood at $11.7 billion at end 1996, exceeded the expected $10.1 billion, the statement said.
"This rapid build-up in reserves was also one of the major elements underlying the very positive investors' confidence in the Philippines," the central bank chief said.
"The balance of payments is expected to sustain a sizeable surplus in 1997 and hence, gross international reserves would be showing a substantial build-up," he added.
Singson said the Central Bank approvals on external borrowings have also been consistently below the ceilings agreed with the IMF in 1996.
